skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-google-ads-conversion-tracking
skill.description: Set up and verify server-side Google Ads purchase tracking for WooCommerce through Product Metrics. Connect the accounts, configure consent, and test delivery to secondary conversion actions.
skill.summary: Connect WooCommerce to Google Ads and verify server-side purchase tracking with Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most flags are Markdown formatting, vendor documentation, or routine setup checks. Real risks include unpinned installation, default remote tool use, account writes without explicit approval, and broad order access. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection or covert data transfer, but the workflow needs stronger limits on credentials, imports, and optional integrations.

remediation.issue: The installation command uses an unpinned executable and mutable skill source.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and skill revision. Require approval before installation and document how to verify both sources.

remediation.issue: The workflow chooses CLI or remote MCP access without a separate approval step and can perform or retry writes.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the CLI and MCP origin before use. Confirm the workspace, store, Google Ads client, and exact change before writing or retrying outside the approved scope.

remediation.issue: Order checks can list recent production orders or retrieve full order details.
remediation.suggestion: Use one approved test order and report only delivery status. Do not list production orders or display customer data for a tracking check.

remediation.issue: The initial order import precedes the consent setup and lacks an explicit data review.
remediation.suggestion: Before import, show the vendor, data fields, date range, and retention terms. Require approval and explain how vendor ingestion differs from Google Ads delivery.

remediation.issue: The references and credential exceptions extend beyond Google Ads conversion tracking.
remediation.suggestion: Mark unrelated features and channels as out of scope. Remove credential exceptions and direct users to enter secrets only through the authorized service interface.

remediation.issue: The skill uses live vendor pages as substitute workflow instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Use reviewed, versioned references. Treat fetched text as data and require separate approval for any new action it proposes.

semantic_findings.title: Order Import Before Data Sharing Review
semantic_findings.description: The guide directs merchants to send initial orders before configuring consent. It describes customer identifiers and costs, but gives no import window or retention details.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The numbered steps place the initial import before consent setup and document identifiers used for customers. They do not establish that Google receives nonconsenting orders.

semantic_findings.title: Reference Steps Extend Beyond the Requested Integration
semantic_findings.description: The skill excludes Enhanced Conversions and other ad channels. Its setup references direct users to connect Meta and ChatGPT Ads and accept Enhanced Conversions terms.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The main workflow points to both connection guides without excluding their extra steps. Those steps can expand platform access beyond the user's request.

semantic_findings.title: Unrelated Credential Exceptions
semantic_findings.description: The secret-handling rule allows requesting Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI credentials and passing them directly to a command. None are required for this Google Ads workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credential exceptions are explicit. The rule does not specify a protected input mechanism, so direct command arguments could appear in process metadata or tool logs.

semantic_findings.title: Live Documentation Used as Workflow Instructions
semantic_findings.description: When bundled references are missing, the skill substitutes remotely fetched Markdown. The pages can change after review without a corresponding skill update.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback treats live pages as equivalent to the local steps and does not pin their contents. No evidence found that those pages contain malicious instructions.

content.user_title: Set Up Google Ads Tracking for WooCommerce
content.value_statement: Browser-based tags can miss purchases, making WooCommerce and Google Ads totals hard to compare. Use Product Metrics to configure server-side tracking and verify delivery with a test order.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status through the configured CLI or MCP and identify the next incomplete step.
Guide WordPress plugin setup, store pairing, and connection to the correct Google Ads client and Merchant Center.
Explain how consent settings and selected paid order statuses affect conversion delivery.
Guide creation of eight secondary actions for revenue, profit, customer segments, and lifetime value.
Verify live order delivery with a paid test order and troubleshoot missing conversions.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a supported WooCommerce setup, and access to Google Ads and its linked Merchant Center.
A person must install the WordPress plugin, enter the setup token, and approve access in Google.
Tracking depends on consent, paid order status, and account configuration. Profit actions require cost data.
Does not set up Enhanced Conversions, Customer Match, or bidding. Only the merchant or advertiser selects primary actions.

use_cases.title: Connect a WooCommerce Store
use_cases.description: Find the account, plugin, consent, and test steps needed to start server-side purchase tracking.

use_cases.title: Compare Purchase Signals
use_cases.description: Check that the new revenue and profit actions are secondary before comparing them with existing purchase tracking.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Missing Conversions
use_cases.description: Check plugin webhooks, paid order statuses, and consent settings when a test purchase does not appear.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: List what I need to connect WooCommerce to Google Ads through Product Metrics. Do not install anything or change settings.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Account Connection
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: the plugin is installed but the accounts are not connected.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through linking my WooCommerce store and Google Ads client account. Tell me which steps I must complete myself. Keep all conversion actions secondary.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Test Purchase
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: tracking is configured but delivery is unverified.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me verify delivery with one approved paid test order. Check webhooks, consent, and order status without listing production orders or displaying customer details.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Tracking Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: a store already has an active purchase action.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my migration plan from browser tracking to Product Metrics. Check account scope, consent, order import, and duplicate counting. Report what needs approval before any changes.

output_examples.input: What should I check before creating conversion actions?
output: Confirm that the WooCommerce store is linked to the Google Ads client account, not the manager account.
Check Merchant Center and Data Manager access. Confirm that the selected consent banner matches the one on your store.
Create the eight actions as secondary so you can compare them with your existing purchase action.

output_examples.input: My paid test order did not verify. What should I check?
output: Check that both plugin webhooks are active and that the test order reached a status marked as paid.
Confirm the configured consent banner and clear the full-page cache after any change.
If the ten-minute verification window expired, start verification again before placing another approved test order.

best_practices: Confirm the intended workspace, storefront, and Google Ads client account before changing connections or conversion actions.
Review the data shared and confirm consent settings before importing orders. Enter one-time tokens directly in WordPress.
Use one approved test order and keep the new actions secondary while comparing them with existing tracking.
anti_patterns: Pasting setup tokens, credentials, or production order details into chat.
Starting a historical import or connecting another ad channel without explicit approval.
Making both revenue and profit primary or removing the existing purchase action before verifying the new setup.

faq.question: Do I need to edit my WordPress theme or DNS?
faq.answer: No. The Product Metrics plugin serves the tracking script and collector from your WordPress site.

faq.question: Do I need Merchant Center?
faq.answer: Yes. Link Merchant Center to the Google Ads client account, then connect it in Product Metrics.

faq.question: Which orders are eligible for conversion tracking?
faq.answer: An order must reach a status you mark as paid. Conversion delivery also depends on the customer's consent.

faq.question: Which consent banners are supported?
faq.answer: The guide lists OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano. Select the banner your store uses.

faq.question: Will setup change what my campaigns use for bidding?
faq.answer: The new conversion actions start as secondary. A person must decide whether to make one primary in Google Ads.

faq.question: Does this set up Enhanced Conversions or Customer Match?
faq.answer: No. This workflow covers server-side purchase tracking. Enhanced Conversions and Customer Match use separate workflows.
